# Content sources, licensing and verification

Accuracy is treated as an engineering requirement:

* nothing is generated by AI and shown as Quran text, translation, tafsir, hadith, grammar or history;
* every dataset is verbatim, attributed and checksummed;
* missing content is shown as missing.

## Bundled (offline) datasets

All of these are in `content/sources/`, byte-exact. Line-ending normalisation is disabled for that folder.

| Dataset | Source | Licence / status | Use in app |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quran text, Uthmani 1.1 | Tanzil Project, tanzil.net | CC BY 3.0 + Tanzil terms (verbatim only, attribute, link to tanzil.net) | Displayed Arabic |
| Quran text, Simple Clean 1.1 | Tanzil | as above | Search index only (lets you search with everyday spelling); never displayed |
| Quran metadata | Tanzil | CC BY 3.0 | Surah names, Meccan/Medinan, revelation order, juz, page, sajdah |
| Translation: Pickthall | M. M. Pickthall, 1930; Tanzil digital text | Public domain (translator d. 1936) | Default translation |
| Translation: Yusuf Ali | A. Yusuf Ali, original 1934–38 text; Tanzil digital text | Public domain in life+70 jurisdictions since 2024 (translator d. 1953). The later revised editions are a different text and are not included | Optional translation |
| English transliteration | Tanzil | Distributed by Tanzil with attribution | Transliteration |
| Morphology v0.4 | Quranic Arabic Corpus (Kais Dukes, University of Leeds) | GNU GPL + corpus terms (verbatim copies, attribute and link). Obtained as a verbatim mirror because the official download asks for an e-mail address; SHA-256 is recorded | Roots, lemmas, part of speech, features |

**Licensing note to review before a store release:** the corpus data is GPL. It ships unmodified as a
separate data file inside the app, with its notice. Get legal advice on whether the app as a whole must be
GPL-licensed, or contact the corpus authors.

### Integrity checks

`tools/build_content.py` checks all of the following and aborts the build if any fails. The results are
in `content/integrity-report.json`.

* 114 surahs; 6,236 verses; sequential numbering.
* Per-surah counts equal the canonical Hafs (Kufan) counts, an independent list in the script.
* Metadata counts and offsets match the text.
* 30 juz markers, 604 pages, 15 sajdah verses.
* Bismillah attribute on ayah 1 of every surah except 1 and 9.
* Every translation covers every verse, with keys aligned.
* Corpus segment and word counts (128,219 segments; 77,429 words). Word alignment with Tanzil tokens:
  6,232 of 6,236 verses. The 4 differences (2:181, 8:6, 13:37, 37:130) come from different word
  segmentation in the two datasets; the app shows the corpus form there, with a note.
* The stored Arabic is byte-identical to the source; a SHA-256 of all verses is stored in the database.

The app's own test suite (`app/test/content_integrity_test.dart`) re-parses the source XML and compares
every one of the 6,236 verses, and re-computes the checksum.

## Loaded online on demand (and cached)

These can be turned off under *You ▸ Online study sources*.

* **Word-by-word glosses and per-word transliteration:** Quran.com API v4 (`api.quran.com`). The app shows
  them only when the gloss count matches the corpus word count for that verse.
* **Classical tafsir, original Arabic:**

  | Scholar | Died | Work |
  |---|---|---|
  | Ibn Kathir | 774 AH | *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim* |
  | al-Tabari | 310 AH | *Jami' al-Bayan* |
  | al-Qurtubi | 671 AH | *al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an* |
  | al-Baghawi | 516 AH | *Ma'alim al-Tanzil* |

  The works are public domain. The text is shown verbatim from the Quran.com digital edition, labelled
  *direct quotation*, with a source link. The digital edition gives no volume or page numbers, and the app
  says so.
* **Recitation:** EveryAyah.com per-verse MP3s:
  * reciters: Alafasy, al-Husary, al-Minshawi (Murattal), Abdul Basit (Murattal);
  * EveryAyah publishes no formal licence. The files are widely used for non-commercial apps; confirm
    permission before any commercial release.

## Linked, not copied (copyrighted)

* Ibn Kathir (abridged English, Darussalam)
* Ma'arif al-Qur'an
* Tafsir al-Jalalayn (English, Aal al-Bayt Institute)

## Not used, and why

| Source | Reason |
|---|---|
| Saheeh International | Copyrighted (Dar Abul-Qasim) |
| Later revised Yusuf Ali editions | Copyrighted |
| Any AI-generated tafsir, context or "occasion of revelation" | Never presented as scholarship |
| Syntactic roles (iʿrāb) | The corpus treebank covers only part of the Quran and has not been integrated; the app says that iʿrāb is not included |

## Reviewed study content (CMS)

* Content types: context, tafsir, reflection, word note, surah intro.
* Every item stores:
  * its category (direct quotation, paraphrase, editorial summary or AI-assisted);
  * its source and scholar;
  * its citation: volume, page, edition and URL;
  * its verse range, version, reviewer and verification date.
* Workflow: `draft → source_verified (editor) → reviewed (reviewer) → approved (reviewer, not the author)
  → published (admin)`.
  * Editing an item resets it to draft and bumps its version.
  * Unpublishing removes it from every device on the next fetch.
* The app stores only items with status `published`, even if a server sent something else.

**Status today:** no CMS study content has been published. The seed creates one *draft*, labelled
AI-assisted, only to show the workflow. Writing and reviewing tafsir summaries and historical context needs
qualified people, and the app is honest about the gap.

## Reflection prompts

The eight general prompts in `app/lib/ui/study.dart` (for example, "Which word or phrase in these verses
stayed with you?") are editorial. They make no claim about meaning, and the app labels them
"not tafsir".
